info.title: eharness team server
info.description: Team-agent server built on eharness (docs/plans/P32-team-example.md). Bearer token auth when TEAM_TOKEN is set; open otherwise.

tags.name: chats
tags.description: The DM chat of an agent: streaming, approvals, resume, history.

Bearer.description: The value of TEAM_TOKEN. Not required when the server runs without one.

model.description: Model id; null = the workspace default.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code (eharness codes pass through).

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes; derived from the name when absent.

role.description: Default `custom`. The lead exists from the seed.

AgentPatch.description: Only the given fields change; `version` bumps.

ChatQueued.description: A turn of this chat runs on another instance: the message was stored in the durable inbox and is steered into it. Follow the turn with `GET /agents/{id}/chat/stream`.

id.description: Chat id of `useChat`; ignored (the chat is the agent DM).

messages.description: Only the **last** message is read: a user message (send), or the assistant message with `approval-responded` / `output-available` tool parts (answers a pending approval; the continuation streams into the same message). Ids, metadata and history of the client are never trusted.

messageId.description: With a user message: replace that message and answer it (edit).

UiMessage.description: An AI SDK `UIMessage`. Stored messages carry `metadata.eharness` (turn id, stop reason, usage, pending approvals).

target.description: `local`: a turn of this instance was aborted; `remote`: the request was written for the instance running it; `idle`: nothing runs.

nextBefore.description: Pass as `before` to load older messages; null = no more.

allOf.description: The summary (kind) message; null when there was nothing to compact.

running.description: A turn runs in this process.

activeTurn.description: The turn running anywhere (any instance), or null.

pending.description: Approvals and questions waiting for the user.

url.description: Use as the `url` of a `file` part of the next user message; the server resolves it to the file content.

get.summary: The fixed tool catalog a definition can choose from

post.summary: Send a message, answer an approval or regenerate (useChat)
post.description:
The body is an AI SDK `useChat` request; the response is the UI message stream (`text/event-stream`).

- **Send**: the last message is a user message. Attachments are `file` parts (`data:` / `https:` URLs, or the `library:///uploads/…` url returned by `POST /library/files`).
- **Approvals**: when a turn ends with an `approval-requested` tool part, the client posts the assistant message back with the part in `approval-responded` (`addToolApprovalResponse` + `sendAutomaticallyWhen`). The continuation streams into the **same** message id.
- **Regenerate / edit**: `trigger: "regenerate-message"`, or a user message with `messageId`.

Busy policy: while a turn of this chat runs, a new user message is **steered** into it (`ifBusy=steer`, default): on this instance the response follows the running turn; when another instance runs it the message goes through the durable inbox and the route answers `202`. `ifBusy=reject` answers `409 EH_SESSION_BUSY` instead. Approvals, regenerate and edit never steer: `409`.

Errors after the turn started (model failure, stale approval answer) arrive as an `error` chunk inside the stream, not as an HTTP status.

get.description: Replays the chunks of the active turn from `from` and follows it until it ends, also when another instance runs it (stream log, ADR-0039). `204` when nothing streams: use the stored messages. A continuation turn after an approval replays only the continuation: refetch the message at the end.

post.summary: Upload a file into the library (/uploads)
post.description: Multipart form with one `file` field (max 10 MB; images, PDF, text, Markdown, CSV, JSON). The file is stored under `/uploads/<day>/…` in the shared library, so agents can read it. Attach it to a message with a `file` part whose `url` is the returned `url`.
